title: Alkami’s Summer 2026 Digital Banking Platform Release
summary: Explore Alkami’s Summer 2026 digital banking platform release. Streamline business approvals, secure open banking data exchange, and automated workflows.
body_text: Driving commercial efficiency, secure data connectivity, and automated workflows with the summer 2026 Digital Banking Platform release. Alkami’s Summer 2026 Digital Banking Platform Release is engineered to accelerate your financial institution’s growth by expanding your digital ecosystem and streamlining high-value workflows. This quarter, we are bringing major enhancements to commercial banking control, introducing seamless open banking connections, and partnering with industry leaders to resolve friction points like fraud and disputes faster than ever before. Elevating the Business and Commercial Banking Experience Winning primary business and commercial relationships requires delivering tools that are both powerful and incredibly efficient to use. This release expands our Business and Commercial Banking Platform functionality to help users maintain absolute control over their liquidity and operations without getting bogged down in administrative friction. Business and Commercial Dashboard Approvals Module Building on our vision of a modular, flexible dashboard library, we are proud to introduce the new Approvals Module. These customized gadgets allow business and commercial users to easily review and authorize high-frequency transaction requests directly from their home screen. To maximize operational efficiency, the dashboard automatically prioritizes and displays the most urgent pending approvals first. Automated Clearing House (ACH) & Wires Authorization Details To further streamline treasury workflows, corporate approvers can now drill into comprehensive ACH and wire payment details directly within the authorization screens. By bringing critical data points immediately into the account holder’s line of sight, this functionality helps businesses significantly reduce manual errors, strengthen internal payment controls, and eliminate unnecessary administrative delays. Automated File Import Mapping & Wire Upload Enhancements Managing mass payment files manually is a recipe for operational bottlenecks. We have unified our high-volume file processing workflows to maximize speed and data integrity across ACH, Wires, and Payee ingestion: ACH, Wire, and Payee File Mapping: Authorized account holders can specify the exact field placement of critical data points across mandatory and optional fields to create, manage, and scale a large library of reusable templates. Built-in search and filter functionality ensures managing complex business and commercial file formats remains effortless. Immediate File Ingestion Validation: To catch errors before they are processed, the Platform instantly cross-references file types, formatting structures, and payment totals right upon upload. Streamlined Wire Uploads: We have enhanced the wire ecosystem with permissions-based functionality, restricting high-value transfers strictly to entitled business and commercial users. The module supports traditional file selection as well as a flexible, efficient drag-and-drop interface for simultaneous, multi-wire submissions. Advanced Risk Mitigation & Financial Reporting Controls Security and financial transparency must evolve together. We’ve rolled out backend, administrative upgrades designed to insulate business and commercial users against insider fraud while optimizing their accounting workflows: Non-Monetary Dual Authorization: To protect businesses from account takeovers, the Platform now enforces strict dual authorization protocols for key non-monetary changes. This includes safeguarding modifications made to client payment methods and updates to internal business and commercial user permissions. Pending Transaction Export Visibility: Businesses can now pull a more complete snapshot of their financial health by including pending transactions directly within their account exports. This significantly boosts real-time visibility into current cash flow and fully supports reporting workflows across various formats, including CSV, OFX, QBO, and QFX formats. Automated Bank Administration Institute Version 2 (BAI2) File Delivery: To support back-office accounting teams, the Platform can now automatically generate and deliver structured financial reporting data in the universally accepted BAI2 file format for seamless backend reconciliation. Explore how these capabilities fit into the broader market by reading about 10 trends shaping business and commercial banking solutions. Expanding the Connected Digital Banking Ecosystem Modern account holders expect their digital banking platform to function as a unified mission control for their financial footprint. This quarter, we have significantly expanded our integrations to bring unmatched flexibility, security, and insight directly into the Digital Banking Platform. Plaid Integration We are thrilled to scale Platform capability with Plaid -powered digital connectivity. This multi-tier integration allows financial institutions to enrich their primary offering across three specific areas: Plaid Auth: Enables instant, secure external account verification, facilitating faster money movement and reducing friction during initial account setup. Plaid Transactions: Supports comprehensive external account aggregation, allowing account holders to view outside balances in one place and positioning your financial institution as their primary financial hub. Plaid Enrich: Automatically scrubs messy raw transaction strings into clean, human-readable descriptions coupled with smart, automated categorization to fuel deeper financial insights. Neural Payments Integration (Embedded P2P) Keeping transaction volumes within your digital perimeter is critical for driving engagement. Our new Neural Payments partnership embeds real-time person-to-person (P2P) money movement directly into the native mobile and online banking experience. Account holders can send or request funds instantly using nothing more than a mobile phone number or email address, providing flexible settlement choices across major networks. Array : Financial Wellness & Identity Protection Deepen account holder value and foster digital loyalty by offering a suite of advanced credit, debt, and identity protection tools deeply integrated with the Alkami Platform: Student Loan Aid: Provides a clear, guided framework to help borrowers navigate complex repayment options and safely reduce their monthly student loan liabilities. Debt Navigator: Offers a centralized, clear overview of consumer debt alongside personalized, intelligent recommendations on pay-down strategies. BuildCredit Rent: Empowers tenants to proactively build positive credit history by reporting on-time rent payments to major credit bureaus. Personal Information Protection: Actively protects consumer privacy by scanning data-broker networks and helping account holders scrub their personal information from public people-search websites. Open Banking: MX & Finicity Integrations Alkami is deeply committed to supporting safe, modern, and open data sharing. Our secure integrations with industry leaders MX and Finicity are fully backed by Financial Data Exchange (FDX) standards. By replacing outdated credential-sharing practices with secure, token-based access utilizing OAuth 2.0 protocols, account holders gain complete control. Financial institutions looking to navigate this shift can read more about managing security, compliance, and risk within open banking to see how these protocols protect user data. Now, account holders can securely set permissions and determine data access limits to third-party applications, as well as easily view or revoke that access at any time directly within your digital banking platform. Zelle® Tile Icon and Text Updates To simplify compliance workflows for your internal teams, Alkami will automatically deploy standardized, approved Zelle® branding across all money movement landing pages. This design enforcement ensures absolute brand consistency regardless of your financial institution’s specific portal theme, helping you effortlessly meet Early Warning Services (EWS) brand audit guidelines. Data & Marketing: Driving Strategic Growth Data is only as powerful as the action it drives. Our latest Data & Marketing Solution release focuses on turning behavioral insights into active growth opportunities for your financial institution. Out-of-the-Box Campaigns: “Ready for Life’s Next Adventure” Following the Financial Fresh Start campaigns launched in March, we are excited to introduce our newest Out-of-the-Box Campaigns, Ready for Life’s Next Adventure . These are built for consumer lending tied to major life events: RV loans, boat and marine loans, and HELOCs for travel or tuition. Pre-built segments identify the life stage, so marketing teams can quickly deploy relevant loan offers without building from scratch. Here’s what that can look like in practice: a $2.7B credit union generated nearly $2.7 million in loan volume over 12 months through boat and RV campaigns alone ($2 million in boats, $680,000 in RVs). Learn more about maximizing these strategies in our report on using digital banking solutions performance data to deepen retail account holder relationships . MANTL: Streamlining Onboarding & Account Opening MANTL continues to evolve Onboarding & Account Opening around four priorities: flexible customer acquisition, configurable decisioning and risk management, operational scale and efficiency, and unified loan origination. In this release, MANTL introduces enhancements designed to help financial institutions deliver a more seamless experience for applicants while giving teams greater control, efficiency, and flexibility behind the scenes. Joint Owner Applications Empowers branch teams to seamlessly capture and add multiple co-applicants to an application right at the start of the origination workflow, improving applicant experience and driving greater branch efficiency. Multi-Authorized Signer Applications Increases efficiency for business and commercial account opening by enabling branch teams to easily input and configure entities during initial application creation. Document Rejection Notifications Speeds up application resolution and reduces manual back-and-forth by sending automated notifications to applicants when an uploaded file is rejected. Expanding the Ecosystem: New Elements Partner(s) The Alkami Elements Partner Program is built for choice and ease, providing financial institutions with agile, cost-effective access to a broad ecosystem of fintech innovators. Financial institutions can quickly deploy specialized tools to meet digital demand without the heavy lift of custom engineering. This quarter, we are proud to announce a new Elements partner: Casap : Fraud and dispute handling are notorious cost centers that historically damage consumer sentiment. Casap is an agentic artificial intelligence platform designed to automate the entire dispute management cycle. Embedded seamlessly within your native Alkami environment, Casap cuts overhead costs for dispute handling, lowers fraud losses, and decreases overall time-to-resolution, keeping account holders happy and clear of the call center. Dive Deeper into the Summer 2026 Digital Banking Platform Release The Summer 2026 release represents our ongoing commitment to helping you serve better and expand relationships smarter. For a deep dive into the technical specifications and to view the full release notes, Alkami customers can visit the Alkami Community. FAQs 1 What's new for business and commercial banking in the Summer 2026 release? The release expands the Business and Commercial Banking Platform with a new dashboard Approvals Module that surfaces the most urgent pending transaction approvals first, drill-in ACH and wire authorization details to reduce manual errors, and unified file-import mapping for ACH, wires, and payees with reusable templates and instant upload validation. It also adds risk controls including non-monetary dual authorization for sensitive changes like payment-method edits and user-permission updates, pending-transaction visibility in account exports (CSV, OFX, QBO, QFX), and automated BAI2 file delivery for back-office reconciliation. 2 What new integrations and connectivity does this release add? It significantly expands the connected ecosystem. Plaid powers external account verification (Auth), outside-balance aggregation (Transactions), and cleaned-up, auto-categorized transaction data (Enrich). A new Neural Payments partnership embeds real-time P2P money movement directly into mobile and online banking using just a phone number or email. Open banking integrations with MX and Finicity are backed by FDX standards and use token-based OAuth 2.0 access, letting account holders set, view, and revoke third-party data permissions inside the platform. Array adds financial-wellness and identity-protection tools such as Student Loan Aid, Debt Navigator, BuildCredit Rent, and personal-information protection. 3 How does the Summer 2026 release help reduce fraud and disputes? Several features target fraud and friction. Non-monetary dual authorization protects against account takeovers by requiring a second approver for key changes to payment methods and user permissions. The new Elements partner Casap is an agentic AI platform embedded in the Alkami environment that automates the full dispute-management cycle, cutting dispute-handling overhead, lowering fraud losses, and shortening time-to-resolution. Standardized Zelle® branding is also auto-deployed across money-movement pages to help meet Early Warning Services brand-audit guidelines. 4 What's new for onboarding, account opening, and marketing? MANTL adds joint-owner applications (capturing multiple co-applicants at the start of origination), multi-authorized-signer support for business and commercial account opening, and automated document-rejection notifications to speed resolution. On the marketing side, the new “Ready for Life’s Next Adventure” out-of-the-box campaigns target consumer lending tied to major life events—RV loans, boat and marine loans, and HELOCs—with pre-built life-stage segments so teams can deploy relevant offers quickly.

title: A full circle moment: From the classroom to Nimble
summary: As a former classroom educator and teacher recruiter, I know how important it is that our kids have effective teachers. When the opportunity to join the Nimble team came across my desk, I was ecstatic — I was being called back home to a mission I'm deeply passionate about.
body_text: As a former classroom educator and teacher recruiter, I know how important it is that our kids have effective teachers. My time in the classroom was formative, difficult, and ultimately life-changing. When I decided 3 years ago to leave the classroom for teacher recruitment, I found myself amid a pandemic hiring season — one that would bring a number of challenges. I faced low applicant volume, numerous bottlenecks in our process, and the occasional principal skirmish over prized applicants! ‍ I knew there had to be a better way to move the strongest candidates through our process faster while ensuring that each principal had a fair shot at staffing their building. My team sought a solution and in the summer of 2021, I was first introduced to Nimble and their founder, Lauren, who had been a teacher recruiter herself at D.C. Public Schools. ‍ After a demo with Lauren, I remember feeling ecstatic about Nimble's potential to drive real change — and I was right. Nimble quickly revolutionized how we brought in talent. ‍ Nimble increased the diversity and size of my applicant pool: Nimble’s easy-to-use application allowed candidates to apply on their phones — something our old ATS had not been able to do. This increased the accessibility of our entire application process. And, because Nimble automatically synced to several big-name job boards (think Indeed, ZipRecruiter, etc.), candidates were quickly made aware that we were hiring. ‍ Nimble provided transparency for principals and reduced bottlenecks: With our old ATS, we’d used spreadsheets to coordinate the process. Nimble’s pooled posting infrastructure and school applications automated this, allowing leaders to submit their vacancies and see where candidates were across the hiring process, even within shared talent pools. This saved me time fumbling through my spreadsheets and built trust among principals in network leadership and the hiring process. ‍ Nimble provided real-time data on my pipelines, vacancies, and hiring progress: Rather than having to craft complex formulas in my spreadsheets, Nimble’s easy-to-access dashboards gave me an at-a-glance view of my pipeline and essential data points like applicant source, diversity metrics, conversion rates, and volume. This allowed me to speak confidently with our principals and other stakeholders on our progress toward being 100% staffed by day one of school. ‍ When the opportunity to join the Nimble team came across my desk, I was ecstatic — I was being called back home to a mission I'm deeply passionate about. I joined the team here at Nimble because I have seen firsthand the impact that this product can have and I deeply believe in its potential to ensure that our kids have strong, effective teachers. ‍

title: zerohash and Marqeta Announce Partnership to Enable Stablecoin Spending Across Global Card Networks
summary: Integration unlocks global stablecoin balances into everyday card spending experiences CHICAGO, July 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- zerohash, a leading infrastructure platform powering crypto, stablecoin, and tokenized asset capabilities for financial institutions, and Marqeta, Inc.
body_text: Integration unlocks global stablecoin balances into everyday card spending experiences CHICAGO, July 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- zerohash , a leading infrastructure platform powering crypto, stablecoin, and tokenized asset capabilities for financial institutions, and Marqeta, Inc . (NASDAQ: MQ), the modern card issuing platform, today announced they will collaborate to integrate zerohash’s stablecoin infrastructure into Marqeta’s flexible card issuing capabilities. The partnership will enable Marqeta customers to embed stablecoin payments directly into new and existing financial products without rebuilding core systems or taking on new regulatory burden. The collaboration comes as stablecoin adoption accelerates across financial services. In February 2026 alone, stablecoin monthly transaction volume hit $7.2 trillion, surpassing the U.S. ACH network ($6.8 trillion) for the first time in history. On zerohash’s platform specifically , transaction volume grew 690% year-over-year in 2025, while transaction frequency was up 208%, underscoring significant growth as stablecoins become embedded in financial workflows. zerohash today supports instant global payouts for platforms including Gusto and Worldpay, as well as real-time account funding for Interactive Brokers, Kalshi, tastytrade, and more. Marqeta has been a trusted partner for crypto-native companies, powering debit card offerings in the U.S. and Europe that enable users to spend in fiat currency based on crypto holdings and earn rewards back in crypto. The partnership will extend Marqeta’s capabilities, allowing both crypto and non-crypto companies to take advantage of the value of stablecoins through this integration. Marqeta’s platform processed nearly $400 billion of payments volume in 2025, while enabling innovative, global payment experiences across diverse use cases. The partnership will let users spend digital dollar balances at tens of millions of merchants globally using a standard payment card. Merchants get paid in fiat currency, just as with any other card transaction. zerohash will provide the underlying infrastructure that handles custody, compliance and liquidity for onchain money custody and movement. Concurrently, Marqeta will manage card issuance, acceptance and bank and network relationships. Together, the integration will give platforms a faster, more flexible way to create spendability for stablecoins with real-time settlement and improved capital efficiency. “Our customers are building the next generation of financial products, and that requires new ways to manage and move money,” said Anthony Peculic, Interim Chief Product Officer at Marqeta. “By integrating with zerohash, we will be able to give our customers a full solution to deliver multinational and stablecoin-backed card programs that meet the needs of their users, while also being compliant and ready for global scale.” “Compatibility between stablecoins and traditional payment networks is a critical unlock for users’ onchain money, while also opening new opportunities for traditional businesses through stablecoin-backed cards,” said Edward Woodford, Founder & CEO of zerohash. “zerohash’s role is to abstract the complexity behind the scenes so stablecoins can be leveraged as a seamless part of everyday payments and money movement.” About zerohash zerohash is a leading infrastructure provider for crypto, stablecoin, and tokenized assets. Its API and embeddable dev-kit enable innovators to easily launch solutions across cross-border payments, commerce, trading, remittance, payroll, tokenization, and on/off-ramps. The company has a global regulatory footprint across the EU, Latin America, Australia, New Zealand, Bermuda, and the U.S., and operates regulated entities in 51 U.S. jurisdictions. For more information, visit zerohash.com. Disclosures zerohash services and product offerings may not be available in all jurisdictions. zerohash accounts are not subject to FDIC or SIPC protections, or any such equivalent protections that may exist outside of the US. zerohash's technical support and enablement of any asset is not an endorsement of such asset and is not a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold any crypto asset. zerohash is not registered with the SEC or FINRA. zerohash llc, NMLS ID #1699379, is licensed as a money transmitter, and zerohash llc and zerohash liquidity services llc are licensed to engage in Virtual Currency Business Activity by the New York State Department of Financial Services. For additional information please visit www.zerohash.com/disclosures . About Marqeta, Inc. Marqeta makes it possible for companies to build and embed financial services into their branded experience—and unlock new ways to grow their business and delight users. The Marqeta platform puts businesses in control of building financial solutions, enabling them to turn real-time data into personalized, optimized solutions for everything from consumer loyalty to capital efficiency. With compliance and security built-in, Marqeta’s platform has been proven at scale, processing nearly $400 billion in annual payments volume in 2025. Marqeta is certified to operate in more than 40 countries worldwide and counting. Visit www.marqeta.com to learn more. title: 7 Best Loxo Alternatives for Recruiting Agencies in 2026
summary: Looking for a Loxo alternative in 2026? Compare 7 recruiting platforms on AI depth, pricing, reports, and support, with honest trade-offs for each.
body_text: TL;DR The 7 best Loxo alternatives in 2026 are Spott (AI-native, contextual matching, branded client reports), Bullhorn (enterprise scale and back-office), Recruiterflow (automation and support quality), Recruit CRM (budget entry point), JobAdder (job board distribution), Vincere (UK/APAC back-office suite), and Ezekia (retained executive search). The right pick depends on whether you're leaving Loxo over pricing trajectory, AI depth, client-facing deliverables, or regional hosting. Why agencies are looking for a Loxo alternative in 2026 Loxo is a genuinely strong product. It scores 4.6 out of 5 on both G2 and Capterra, its built-in sourcing database of roughly 1.2 billion profiles is the most differentiated feature in the category, and reviewers consistently say it feels "built by recruiters for recruiters." For US agencies whose biggest constraint is outbound sourcing volume, it earns its reputation. The reasons agencies evaluate alternatives in 2026 cluster around four themes. The pricing trajectory. Loxo's Basic plan is now $169 per user per month, and Professional contracts typically land between $250 and $400 per user per month depending on seat count and modules. Multiple Capterra reviewers report automatic 5% annual price increases written into contracts, and contact-credit overage pricing isn't publicly disclosed. The free tier is a great entry point. The exit trajectory is what catches agencies off guard. Client-facing deliverables under-deliver. Reviewers flag resume formatting and CRM function as weak spots, and Loxo's candidate report output has historically been a sore point. When the document you send a client is the product of your work, that matters. Integrations feel bolted together. Several G2 reviewers describe Loxo's integrations as "clunky and half-baked," with some requiring paid add-ons or custom development. Agencies running omnichannel outreach across email, LinkedIn, and WhatsApp tend to hit these edges first. Support and hosting. Loxo's support is chatbot-first, and users report that reaching a human takes effort. The platform is also US-centric, with limited regional data residency for European agencies with GDPR-driven hosting requirements. If any of that resonates, the seven platforms below are the alternatives most often shortlisted against Loxo in 2026. Comparison at a glance Platform Best for Distinct strength Spott Agencies wanting AI built into every workflow Contextual AI matching, branded reports, omnichannel inbox Bullhorn Large staffing firms with back-office needs Scale, VMS integrations, ecosystem Recruiterflow Small-to-mid agencies focused on automation Automation maturity, support quality Recruit CRM Cost-sensitive teams under 20 seats Entry pricing, fast setup JobAdder ANZ/UK agencies leaning on job boards 200+ board ecosystem Vincere UK/APAC temp and contract operations Back-office depth, analytics Ezekia Retained executive search firms Assignment management, client portals Loxo US agencies constrained by sourcing volume 1.2B-profile sourcing database How we evaluated each platform The platforms below were assessed against five criteria that consistently come up when agencies tell us why they're moving off Loxo: AI depth. Is AI part of the core data model, or a layer for sourcing only? Does it understand context (notes, calls, messages) or just keywords? Total cost trajectory. Not the entry price, but what you'll actually pay in year two and three once credits, modules, and indexation kick in. Client deliverables. Can you send a client a candidate report in your own branding without rebuilding it in Word? Workflow fit by staffing model. Perm, temp, contract, and retained search have different needs. Support and hosting. Can you reach a human, and can you host data where your compliance team needs it? Pricing is quoted from public information and recent reviews. Always confirm current pricing with the vendor before signing. 1. Spott Founded: 2024 | HQ: San Francisco | Pricing: From $139/user/month Spott is an AI-native ATS/CRM built from inception around AI rather than retrofitted with it. Where Loxo's AI focuses on sourcing, Spott's AI runs through the entire workflow: matching that reads context (full work history, notes, call transcripts, messages) instead of keywords, an AI notetaker that updates candidate profiles automatically, data enrichment , outreach campaigns across email and WhatsApp, and analytics, all in one seat price. Where Spott stands out vs Loxo: Client deliverables you'd actually send. Spott generates candidate presentation reports in your own Word or PowerPoint templates. Loxo's report output is a recurring complaint in user reviews. Pricing that holds. One transparent seat price with matching, notetaking, and reports included. No credit-overage surprises, no automatic annual indexation written into the contract. Searchable context. Notes, transcripts, and messages are searchable and feed the AI matching. Ask a natural-language question ("who did we interview last year with pricing experience in SaaS?") and get an answer, not a saved-search project. EU hosting and ISO 27001. EU-hosted option, GDPR compliant, ISO 27001 certified. For European agencies, this is a structural difference, not a checkbox. Human support. Direct access to the team, with a roadmap that ships weekly. "The precision of the AI matching stood out immediately." — Kristof Stevens, United Consulting What to keep in mind: No built-in sourcing database. Loxo Source's 1.2B profiles have no direct equivalent in Spott; sourcing runs through LinkedIn Recruiter and enrichment instead. No native VoIP or SMS module; Spott integrates with VoIP providers rather than running telephony in-house. Founded in 2024, so it's the youngest platform on this list, backed by Y Combinator and shipping weekly. Best for: Agencies of 5-200 recruiters running perm, contract, or retained search who want AI in the whole workflow, branded client deliverables, and a price that doesn't escalate. Bottom line: If you're leaving Loxo over pricing trajectory, report quality, or AI that stops at sourcing, Spott is the most direct answer. For a side-by-side breakdown, see the full Spott vs Loxo comparison . 2. Bullhorn Founded: 1999 | HQ: Boston | Pricing: Starter $99/user/mo, Core $165/user/mo (published, July 2026); Pro and add-ons quote-only Bullhorn is the legacy market leader: 10,000+ customers, 300+ integrations, and a proven track record at 500+ seat firms. Where Bullhorn stands out vs Loxo: enterprise scale, deep temp/contract back-office (timesheets, pay & bill, 110+ VMS integrations), and the Amplify AI suite, which is the most substantive AI investment among legacy vendors. What to keep in mind: the seat price is not the total cost. Automation, analytics, and Amplify are typically priced as separate modules, buyer reports and reviews cite implementation fees in the low thousands, and customers report annual price indexation in multi-year contracts. Reviews consistently flag slow, dense UX and support queues. Best for: Larger staffing firms with VMS-driven contracts and serious back-office requirements. Bottom line: The move if you're outgrowing Loxo into enterprise temp/contract. Budget for the add-ons. Side-by-side detail in our Spott vs Bullhorn comparison . 3. Recruiterflow Founded: 2016 | HQ: San Francisco | Pricing: From $119/user/month, AIRA plan around $149/user/month Recruiterflow serves 1,700+ agencies and built its name on automation and unusually good support (responses often within minutes, per reviewers). Where Recruiterflow stands out vs Loxo: automation maturity (years of battle-tested sequences and triggers), bundled AI (the AIRA plan includes all current and future agents at one price), and a support reputation that is the opposite of chatbot-first. What to keep in mind: US-hosted only, which rules it out for agencies with EU residency requirements. AIRA is a recent layer on an automation-first product, and LinkedIn messages aren't a native sequence step. Contacts and candidates live as separate records. Best for: Small-to-mid US agencies (10-50 recruiters) that prioritize workflow automation and responsive support. Bottom line: The strongest support-and-automation story on this list. Feature-level breakdown in our Spott vs Recruiterflow comparison . 4. Recruit CRM Founded: 2017 | HQ: New Jersey | Pricing: Pro $85, Business $125, Enterprise $165/user/month Recruit CRM is the budget-conscious pick, used in 100+ countries with strong review scores and a setup most users describe in hours, not days. Where Recruit CRM stands out vs Loxo: entry pricing at half of Loxo's Basic plan, an unlimited free trial, fast onboarding, and native VoIP via Twilio. What to keep in mind: AI depth trails the AI-native platforms (parsing plus bimetric scoring rather than contextual matching), agencies report configurability and reporting ceilings past 20-30 users, and features like open API access sit on higher tiers. Best for: Small agencies under 20 recruiters that want the basics done well at an accessible price. Bottom line: If Loxo's price is the only reason you're leaving, Recruit CRM is the cheapest credible landing spot. Expect to outgrow it. Details in our Spott vs Recruit CRM comparison . 5. JobAdder Founded: 2007 | HQ: Sydney | Pricing: ~$135-160+/user/month, custom quotes JobAdder brings 26,000+ users, a clean interface, and a 200+ job board ecosystem including native SEEK integration. Where JobAdder stands out vs Loxo: job board distribution breadth (the inverse of Loxo's outbound-sourcing strength), an 18-year track record with 99% CSAT, and a dedicated in-house recruitment edition. What to keep in mind: AI arrived late (Adder Intelligence launched November 2025) and requires the Essential plan or higher. Reporting depth is the most-flagged weakness in reviews, and the European footprint outside the UK is thin. Best for: ANZ and UK agencies whose sourcing strategy runs on job board distribution rather than outbound. Bottom line: A sensible swap only if your sourcing model is inbound. Full comparison in our Spott vs JobAdder comparison . 6. Vincere Founded: 2012 | Owned by: The Access Group | Pricing: From £69/user/month, AI Copilot from £25/agency/month Vincere is a full-stack recruitment operating system with CRM, ATS, analytics, and genuine back-office (timesheets, pay & bill, invoicing), strongest in the UK and APAC. Where Vincere stands out vs Loxo: back-office depth Loxo doesn't attempt, 50+ built-in reports, and sharper entry pricing than it had two years ago. What to keep in mind: post-acquisition customer experience under Access Group is a recurring review theme (support responsiveness, contract renewal practices), releases are quarterly at best, and modular pricing complicates budgeting. Best for: UK/APAC agencies running temp and contract that need integrated back-office. Bottom line: The like-for-like choice for temp-heavy UK/APAC operations, with the Access Group ownership as the asterisk. Side-by-side in our Spott vs Vincere comparison . 7. Ezekia Founded: 2015 | HQ: London | Pricing: ~£120/user/month Ezekia is purpose-built for retained executive search: assignment management, polished client portals, BD pipelines, and branded reporting, with 550+ firms and a 99.7% retention rate. Where Ezekia stands out vs Loxo: the exec-search workflow is native rather than adapted, and the client portal experience is the most polished in this list. Loxo serves exec search, but as one model among many. What to keep in mind: Ezekia covers retained exec search only; perm, temp, and contracting are out of scope. It added OpenAI-based features but isn't AI-native, integrations are limited (Outlook, Zapier), and migration fees have been reported as high as £5,000. Best for: Boutique retained executive search firms that want depth in one model. Bottom line: The specialist play. If your firm is 100% retained search and Loxo feels generic, Ezekia fits like a glove; if you run mixed models, it can't follow you. More in our Spott vs Ezekia comparison . When Loxo is still the right call Not every Loxo customer should leave. Loxo remains your best option if outbound sourcing volume is your defining constraint and the 1.2B-profile database genuinely replaces a separate sourcing stack for you, you're US-based with no EU hosting requirements, and your contract economics still work after factoring in the annual increases. The sourcing database is the killer feature, and nothing on this list replaces it one-for-one. If sourcing isn't your bottleneck, though, you're paying a premium for a database you don't fully use, and the alternatives above will likely fit better. How to choose your Loxo alternative If AI depth is the driver: Spott is the most AI-native option on this list, with matching, notes, reports, and outreach designed around AI from inception rather than added to a sourcing tool. If you're enterprise temp/contract: Bullhorn or Vincere. Bullhorn for VMS depth and ecosystem, Vincere for sharper pricing and analytics. If you're cost-driven: Recruit CRM at $85/user/month, with the scalability ceiling as the known trade-off. If support quality burned you: Recruiterflow's human, fast support is the strongest contrast to chatbot-first service. If you're retained exec search only: Ezekia. If EU hosting and GDPR are non-negotiable: Spott (EU-hosted, ISO 27001) is the clearest fit; most other options on this list are US-hosted. Related reading Top Bullhorn alternatives for agencies in 2026 Recruitment CRM migration: the 4-week playbook The bottom line Loxo earned its reputation on sourcing, and for agencies whose growth is gated by outbound volume, it still delivers. But if your bills keep climbing while the AI stops at sourcing, your client reports need rework before every send, and support means arguing with a chatbot, the market has moved. If you want to see what an AI-native ATS/CRM does across your whole workflow, not just sourcing, book a Spott demo . Migration is handled in-house by our team, go-live takes a day to a few weeks, depending on database size and feedback speed, and the AI is in the seat price, not the next tier up. Research current as of June 2026. Pricing and feature claims are based on vendor websites and publicly available reviews at the time of writing. Always confirm current pricing directly with the vendor.

title: Telix Doses First Patient in Phase 3 LUTEON Trial of TLX250-Txfor Renal Cancer
summary: Our mission is to help patients with cancer live longer with better quality lives
body_text: Telix Doses First Patient in Phase 3 LUTEON Trial of TLX250-Tx for Renal Cancer Melbourne (Australia) and Indianapolis, IN (United States) | July 21, 2026 First patient dosed in Phase 3 LUTEON [1] trial evaluating TLX250-Tx in relapsed or recurrent clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). LUTEON is the first Phase 3 study of a CAIX [2] -targeted radiopharmaceutical therapy in ccRCC. Telix today announced that the first patient has been dosed with TLX250-Tx (lutetium-177 (177Lu) girentuximab tetraxetan) in the LUTEON study, the first radiopharmaceutical therapy to enter Phase 3 development for ccRCC. LUTEON is a randomized, prospective, open label, multi-center study evaluating a CAIX-targeting radionuclide therapy in patients with relapsed or recurrent ccRCC. The patient was dosed at GenesisCare Murdoch (Western Australia), under the supervision of Dr. Aviral Singh. Dr. Aviral Singh, Clinical Head of Theranostics and Nuclear Medicine at GenesisCare Murdoch and Principal Investigator on the LUTEON trial, commented, “Dosing the first patient in the LUTEON study marks an important milestone in the development of potential new treatment options for patients with relapsed or recurrent clear cell renal cell carcinoma. Despite advances in care, outcomes remain poor for many patients, underscoring the need for innovative therapeutic approaches. This study will play a critical role in evaluating the safety, tolerability and efficacy of this investigational CAIX-targeted radiopharmaceutical for patients globally, and we look forward to helping advance the clinical evidence for this promising therapeutic candidate.” Dr. David N. Cade, Telix Group Chief Medical Officer, added, “LUTEON represents the next stage in Telix’s global clinical development of TLX250-Tx and reflects our commitment to developing precision radiopharmaceuticals for patients with difficult-to-treat cancers. We aim to further evaluate the potential of TLX250-Tx that is designed to utilize the high prevalence of CAIX expression in ccRCC to deliver targeted radiation directly to tumor sites, while limiting exposure to healthy tissue.” About TLX250-Tx TLX250-Tx is a first-in-class CAIX-targeting rADC [3] therapy candidate composed of a high-specificity monoclonal antibody chelated to the therapeutic radionuclide lutetium-177. CAIX is an attractive therapeutic target because it is expressed in more than 95% of ccRCC, while demonstrating limited expression in normal tissues, including kidney tissue [4] , [5] . LUTEON is being run under a Phase 3 protocol in Australia and forms part of Telix’s global development program for TLX250-Tx, which includes the separate Phase 2a LUTEON ATLAS study in the United States and Europe. The LUTEON study utilizes Telix’s investigational PET [6] imaging agent, TLX250-Px (Zircaix® [7] , zirconium-89 (89Zr) girentuximab senvedoxam), to identify eligible patients with CAIX-positive tumors. About clear cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Renal Cell Carcinoma, RCC, is the most common form of kidney cancer, accounting for approximately 9 out of 10 diagnoses [8] . Within this category, ccRCC is the most common and often the most aggressive subtype, representing about 85% of all RCC cases [9] with up to 30% of patients presented with metastatic disease at diagnosis, which has a 20% 5-year survival rate [10] , [11] . TLX250-Tx and TLX250-Px have not received a marketing authorization in any jurisdiction. [1] ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT07197580 . [2] Carbonic Anhydrase IX. [3] Radio antibody-drug conjugate. [4] Luong-Player A, et al. Am J Clin Pathol. 2014. [5] Kleinendorst SC, et al. Theranostics. 2024. [6] Positron emission tomography. [7] Brand name subject to final regulatory approval. [8] Bukavina, L, et al. Eur Urol . 2022. [9] Alchahin AM, et al. Nat Commun. 2022. [10] National Cancer Institute. Cancer stat facts: kidney and renal pelvis cancer. Updated 2025. Accessed May 1, 2026. https://seer.cancer.gov/statfacts/html/kidrp.html. [11] Vento JA, et al. Cancers (Basel) . 2022.

title: AI as your personal journalist
summary: Since the boom of GPT, one year ago, at Slite we kept playing with it and other AI functionalities to help us fix pain points our users and we are facing with knowledge base.
body_text: Since the boom of GPT, one year ago, at Slite we realized a great opportunity that AI brought and ever since then, we started building the first company knowledge base on autopilot. We kept playing with it and other AI functionalities to help us fix pain points our users and we are facing with knowledge base. Although we wanted as much as possible to avoid going in the dark side of content generation we finally gave it a try to kickstart Slite organization onboarding with a nice personalized suggestion of structure for your knowledge base. Writer's block Imagine you want to organize knowledge for your new company, for your team or even for a personal project you want to share with the world. Filled with determination, you open your favorite editor and... Nothing comes up, or too many things maybe ? Of course you are not a writer! Building a structure is hard: which topic should we start with ? so many possibilities, which one is the best ? The good news is: there is no perfect structure, everything will keep moving, you just need a little help to start (then help maintaining it). At Slite we think this is exactly this kind of situation where GPT content could shine: Nothing is right or wrong It can be quickly approved or denied It's hyper customized GPT as a journalist If you already used ChatGPT, you know the experience is mostly you asking questions and it answering to you the best it can. For our wiki generator side project, we wanted to experiment with the opposite pattern: in the manner of a journalist, GPT would lead the discussion, asking you as many question as it could, bouncing on your answers, to slowly go deeper in your thoughts, trying to extract your raw ideas into structure and content. System prompt 🧠 You are a famous journalist expert in structureType. Your role is to ask questions to the user so they can build a tree structure to organize their knowledge about structureType. You should be nice and fun, don't push the user too hard, ask simple and clear questions to learn about the user needs. You can ask details to propose more sub sections to produce a deeper tree. Answer in casual discussion style, with few sentences. You must ask only one question at a time. Nothing fancy here, following prompt principle for instructions we turn GPT into a journalist expert in your domain. Then few directives we adapted while playing with it to obtain something not too overwhelming (especially GPT-4 tends to ask you dozens of questions at once which could lead you back to your starting "writer's block" point). Reverse ChatGPT If you've developed a bit with OpenAI Chat Completions API : "The main input is the messages parameter. Messages must be an array of message objects, where each object has a role (either "system", "user", or "assistant") and content. Conversations can be as short as one message or many back and forth turns. Typically, a conversation is formatted with a system message first, followed by alternating user and assistant messages." To fit this standard we will need to mimic a starting conversation between the user and the assistant. It will also help the journalist and the user to know each other and skip the formality for our real user. 🧚 Hi, I need help to produce a tree structure for my knowledge about structureType. Please always give me examples. Answer in casual discussion style, with few sentences. 🤖 Hello! I'd be happy to assist you with setting up a structure about structureType. Okay, let's start with a simple question. First, can you share with me why you want to build a structure about structureType? Who is your audience? What is your goal? If you have tried our now retired Wiki generator in thr past you will recognize it. This is indeed the first message the bot always sends you when you start the conversation (but you don't know we also mimicked your first message 🧚). These 3 ice breaking questions are usually enough to unlock the situation and awake the journalist inside GPT. It will then keep asking you questions as long as you keep answering them. Freelance journalist Now we have a nice interview of our user, but we still don't have any structure nor content. That's where a 3rd protagonist appear: Between each exchange of the discussion, another prompt is triggered to produce the structure based on the discussion. 🧠 You are a famous journalist expert in structureType. Your role is to build a tree structure to organize user knowledge about structureType. System prompt is simpler this time, there is no need to do the "interview" part. Then we will mimic one more exchange between the assistant and the user to be able to trigger one more invisible request from the user. 🧚 Yes, let's create types section with timple types ‍ 🤖 ok 🧚 Based on our discussion and my instructions, can you propose me a custom structure to organize my knowledge about structureType ? It should be recursive JSON. For example: { "Title": { "Section 1": { }, "Section 2": { "Subsection 1": {}, "Subsection 2": {}, }, "Section 3": { "Subsection A": {}, "Subsection B": {}, }, "Section 4": { "Subsection X": {}, "Subsection Y": {}, }, } } ‍ ‍ This is the user mimicked prompt for the first sidebar generation as we need to give an example of the format to GPT. The challenge now is to keep showing things to the user so that they don't feel the waiting time. So we are using the JSON mode of the completion API in combination with partial json parser to be able to stream the sidebar while it's built by OpenAI. No need to say that having a proper JSON answer is awesome from a developer perspective as we can easily convert it to any UI. We also have a simple AI to suggest icons but as you can see it's more adapted to company knowledge base than Pokemon. Going back to the discussion Now we have a problem: we kind of forked the discussion to another purpose. We need to be able to continue the discussion while letting the first journalist know about the resulting structure so it can bounce from it. Again this time we will mimic another exchange between the user and the assistant. 🤖 Here is a structure proposition: JSON.stringify(newStructure) 🧚 ok, help me to continue to build my knowledge base structure by continuing the discussion. Answer in casual discussion style, with few sentences. Now GPT journalist knows/thinks it already produced a structure and will be able to reference it to continue the discussion. By using this technique, we give the illusion of only one ongoing discussion! We haven't deployed this version yet but it also opens the possibility for the user to modify the structure by hand in parallel of the discussion (moving or deleting part of it for example). Indeed the parts in the dotted squares of the schema are not persisted in the conversation history. The next time the user answer to the journalist, we will also send the current state of the structure to the freelancer. Here is the variant of the mimicked user prompt to pass the current structure: 🧚 Here is the current structure: JSON.stringify(structure) Can you adapt it following my latest instructions ? Answer with a recursive JSON structure. This can continue over and over, we also save tokens by not persisting all the JSON structure evolution. Conclusion If you played with our wiki generator a bit, you will quickly see the limit of this technique. GPT-4 tend to ignore a bit when you say no to the suggestion. It's also not adapted if you start to ask questions yourself. Indeed we kind of force it to always produce a structure and continue from the discussion based on this new structure. A solution for that may be to use OpenAI function calling to let it decide if it should call the function callFreelancer for example with tool_choice: "auto" . It may also simplify the back and forth as the main journalist would know it asked for the freelancer's help, but we still need to explore this... What we've learned specifically with this experiment is that it's great to use it as a kind of reverse ChatGPT to push the user to formalize something usually boring (like onboarding forms) by asking it human questions. It's also ok to alter the history of a prompt and inject mimicked part of the discussion to maintain it in a certain direction (a bit like stable diffusion prompt editing technique ). Last but not least, OpenAI functions (called tools now) could also serve as a way to trigger some specific paths for the discussion or call other assistants, not only calling external functions. Bonus We also added a template generator when you click on a document in the sidebar. This one is quite simple, we pass the discussion and the structure to an assistant along with a prompt describing the different format of blocks it can use. 🧚 Now can you give me a template example to fill the content of a document ? A template is a JSON array of blocks. A block is a JSON object with a "type" field and a "data" field. Type should be exclusively picked in the list: listOfSupportedTypes Type1 is [...] Type2 is [...] [...] For example: templateBlocksExample I want a template for the document Path/To/The document

title: Fixed a panic in project metrics collection that could drop metrics
summary: Fixed a panic in project metrics collection that could drop metrics
body_text: The privileged metrics endpoint could intermittently panic while serving concurrent requests, because a single parser instance was shared across those requests instead of each request getting its own. The panic stopped metrics collection for the affected project until the metrics service restarted. Each request now gets its own parser instance, so concurrent metrics requests no longer interfere with each other.
